answer: Deterministic namespace mining. Each new identity must claim an unused name keyed to its public key by solving a fixed hash puzzle; the first claimant of a name wins a permanent meadow of unique handles. Cloning forces attackers to solve a fresh puzzle per identity at real compute cost, while honest agents solve once and reuse their namespace as a relic of past work. Verified uniqueness gives newcomers a haven from duplicate-name collisions, so copying an established handle fails outright.
